item.title: Shingen Mochi: Yamanashi's Beloved Kinako-and-Syrup Sweet — Guide
item.description: Shingen mochi is one of Yamanashi’s most beloved local sweets, consisting of soft, chewy rice cake (mochi) generously dusted with kinako (roasted soybean flour) and served with a small pot of kuromitsu (black sugar syrup) to drizzle over the top. Named after the region’s revered samurai warlord Takeda Shingen, the sweet is sold in distinctive small boxes wrapped in a furoshiki cloth, and its combination of nutty soybean flour, chewy mochi and rich dark syrup makes it a popular souvenir and teatime treat.
